predecessors.name: Ahar–Banas culture
predecessors.text: the Malwa-plateau part of the Ahar country; 'preceded by the Kayatha, Ahar-Banas, and Savalda cultures'

successors.name: Jorwe culture
successors.text: 'succeeded by the Jorwe culture and the Black and red ware culture'; the Jorwe page: 'preceded by the Malwa culture' and 'also reached north into the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh'

ledger.x: c. 1600 BCE: the Malwa Chalcolithic culture stands on the Malwa plateau and in the north Deccan. 'It is mainly dated to c. 1600 - c. 1300 BCE' (the beginning 'may be as early as c. 2000-1750 BCE'); 'existed in the Malwa region of Central India and parts of Maharashtra in the Deccan Peninsula'. The year is the page's…

c. 1600 BCE: the Malwa culture takes over the Malwa-plateau sites of the Ahar-Banas culture (Mandsaur, Kayatha). 'preceded by the Kayatha, Ahar-Banas, and Savalda cultures'; no page dates the handover.

c. 1400 BCE: the Maharashtra sites pass to the Jorwe culture. The Jorwe page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorwe_culture) dates its early phase 'c. 1400-1000 BCE' and names Daimabad and Inamgaon among its sites; the Malwa page lists the same two among its own. Both pages name the sites; neither dates the handover.

c. 1300 BCE: the Malwa culture gives way to the Jorwe culture. 'It is mainly dated to c. 1600 - c. 1300 BCE', 'succeeded by the Jorwe culture and the Black and red ware culture'. The page gives no phases and no account of the end.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture known from eight named sites; the page names no rivers or districts.
